name: Grok Build

model.note: Grok Build names full model ids (grok-build, grok-4.6) and publishes no tier naming to map onto, so only an explicit per-harness pin is emitted.

skills.notes: Walks `.grok/skills` up to the repo root and reads Claude Code skills alongside; `.agents/skills` is documented at user level only, so it is not the install target here.

notes: Agents are Markdown + YAML frontmatter in .grok/agents/ (user level ~/.grok/agents/), and the parent reaches one with the spawn_subagent tool. The documented frontmatter is name, description, model, tools, mcpInheritance, permissionMode. `tools` is omitted deliberately: the documented example mixes MCP tool ids with Claude-style names, and an allowlist written from a guess would silently strip the role's tools. Read-only therefore rides on the prompt; where it must be enforced, add a .grok/roles/<name>.toml with default_capability_mode = "read-only" and point the agent at it. Grok Build reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md plus .grok/rules/ and .claude/rules/, so `waypost agents register` reaches it. No `env` markers: every documented GROK_* variable is a user-set config knob (GROK_HOME, GROK_THEME, feature flags), not something the harness sets for its own session — attributing a commit on one would be a guess, so a session in Grok Build labels itself with WAYPOST_HARNESS=grok.
